title: A True Story of Sea Turtles

topics.name: Adjective clauses: who, which, whose, where
Main and subordinate clauses: when, as soon as, until, unless
Linking words: however, therefore, although, despite

options: The volunteer which found the egg shells told us at once.
The volunteer who found the egg shells told us at once.
The volunteer who he found the egg shells told us at once.
questions.rule: For a person, the adjective clause begins with who, and who is already the subject, so no extra 'he'.

options: The eggs was laid in a deep pit.
The eggs were lay in a deep pit.
The eggs were laid in a deep pit.
questions.rule: Passive = be + past participle. Plural 'eggs' takes were, and the participle of lay is laid.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Inside the clause the subject is she (singular), and birth is in the past: she was born.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: In the passive, were is followed by the past participle: were protected.
Plural subject 'sea turtles' + passive in the present: are protected.

questions.before: The beach was closed to the public,
questions.rule: The second idea is the result of the first, so join with so. 'despite' needs a noun, and 'however' cannot join clauses with a comma.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with an adjective clause.
questions.rule: where turtles nest is an adjective clause telling us more about 'the beach'.

chat: When did the baby turtles hatch?
options: They hatched when the sun was came up.
They hatch when the sun come up.
They hatched when the sun came up.
questions.rule: Both clauses tell about a past event, so both use the simple past: hatched ... came up.

chat: Who made this short film on turtles?
options: It was make by our school club.
It made by our school club.
It was made by our school club.
questions.rule: Past passive = was/were + past participle: It was made by ...

options: The nests were protected by the villagers.
The nests are protected by the villagers.
The nests are protect by the villagers.
questions.rule: Simple present active becomes am/is/are + past participle: are protected. Keep the same tense.

options: As soon as the eggs were laid, the turtle went back to the sea.
As soon as the eggs were laid, so the turtle went back to the sea.
As soon the eggs were laid, the turtle went back to the sea.
questions.rule: The linker is as soon as (three words), and the main clause needs no extra 'so'.

options: Despite of the heavy rain, the volunteers walked along the beach.
Despite the heavy rain, the volunteers walked along the beach.
Despite it rained heavily, the volunteers walked along the beach.
questions.rule: Despite is followed directly by a noun phrase (no 'of', no full clause): Despite the heavy rain.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: For a person who does the action, use who, not 'which'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The main clause is in the past (stayed), so the 'until' clause is also past: reached.

questions.after: shell was olive green, came ashore at night.
questions.rule: whose shows possession (her shell). 'who's' means 'who is'.

questions.after: the turtle has laid her eggs, she covers them with sand.
questions.rule: As soon as starts a time clause with normal word order. 'No sooner' and 'Hardly' need 'had/does' and 'than/when'.
Passive: subject + were + past participle buried.

chat: Did you see the hatchlings at Velas?
options: No, we reached late; although, the guide showed us a video.
No, we reached late; however, the guide showed us a video.
No, we reached late, despite the guide showed us a video.
questions.rule: however, links two sentences after a semicolon. 'Although' and 'despite' cannot be used like this.

questions.source: The eggs hatched. The hatchlings rushed to the sea.
options: As soon as the eggs hatched, the hatchlings rush to the sea.
As soon as the eggs hatched, the hatchlings rushed to the sea.
As soon as the eggs hatched, then the hatchlings rushed to the sea.
questions.rule: As soon as joins the clauses; keep both in the past and do not add 'then'.

questions.source: The villagers offer homestays. They help protect the turtles.
options: The villagers who offer homestays they help protect the turtles.
The villagers who offer homestays help protect the turtles.
The villagers who offers homestays help protect the turtles.
questions.rule: who replaces 'They', so drop 'they'. 'who' refers to 'villagers' (plural), so the verb is offer.

options: Velas, that is in Ratnagiri district, is famous for its turtles.
Velas, which is in Ratnagiri district, is famous for its turtles.
Velas, which is in Ratnagiri district, are famous for its turtles.
questions.rule: Between commas (extra information) use which, not 'that'. Velas is one place, so is famous.

options: A booklet on turtles is being printed this week.
A booklet on turtles is being print this week.
A booklet on turtles is been printed this week.
questions.rule: Present continuous passive = is/are being + past participle: is being printed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A full clause (she was sleepy) needs although. 'Despite' takes a noun or -ing form.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The subject Both nests is plural, so the passive helper is were.

questions.before: By the end of that season, more than fifty nests
questions.rule: 'By the end of that season' looks back from the past: past perfect passive had been protected.
The subordinate clause Although it was raining comes first, followed by a comma and the main clause.

chat: Which turtles nest on our Konkan coast?
options: Mostly Olive Ridleys, who's babies hatch in about fifty days.
Mostly Olive Ridleys, which babies hatch in about fifty days.
Mostly Olive Ridleys, whose babies hatch in about fifty days.
questions.rule: To show possession (their babies), use whose.

chat: Why did the villagers stop stealing eggs?
options: Tourism brought them income; therefore they protects the nests now.
Tourism brought them income; despite, they started protecting the nests.
Tourism brought them income; therefore, they began to protect the nests.
questions.rule: therefore, introduces a result. 'they protects' breaks agreement, and 'despite' cannot link two sentences.

questions.source: Although the hatchlings were tiny, they faced the waves bravely.
options: Despite the hatchlings were tiny, they faced the waves bravely.
Despite of being tiny, the hatchlings faced the waves bravely.
Despite being tiny, the hatchlings faced the waves bravely.
questions.rule: Despite + -ing form (no 'of'): Despite being tiny, ...

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: The subject is The guide (singular, past): was. A place where something happens takes where.

options: If the volunteers had not acted, the turtles would disappeared from Konkan.
If the volunteers have not acted, the turtles would have disappeared from Konkan.
If the volunteers had not acted, the turtles would have disappeared from Konkan.
questions.rule: Third conditional: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Every volunteer is singular, so the main verb is has to. The clause 'who joins the camp' does not change that.

questions.before: Each of the families that offer homestays
questions.after: ten per cent to the fund.
questions.rule: Each of + plural noun takes a singular verb: Each ... gives.

questions.after: no experience, the team started a turtle project.
questions.rule: After despite, use a noun or an -ing form: Despite having.

questions.prompt: Make a present perfect passive sentence.
questions.rule: Present perfect passive = has/have been + past participle: has been visited.

chat: Has the homestay room been cleaned for the guests?
options: Yes, it has just be cleaned.
Yes, it have just been cleaned.
Yes, it has just been cleaned.
questions.rule: Present perfect passive: it has been cleaned. 'it' takes has, and after 'has' we need been.

chat: Will you call me when the eggs hatch?
options: Sure, I will call you as soon as they hatch.
Sure, I will call you as soon as they will hatch.
Sure, I call you as soon as they hatched.
questions.rule: In a time clause about the future, use the simple present (as soon as they hatch), not 'will'.

questions.source: If people do not protect the nests, the turtles will die out.
options: Unless people protect the nests, the turtles will die out.
Unless people do not protect the nests, the turtles will die out.
Unless people protected the nests, the turtles will die out.
questions.rule: Unless means 'if ... not', so drop 'do not' and keep the present tense: Unless people protect.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Plural they keep (a general truth). 'In 2005' is past and 'hundreds of eggs' is plural: were stolen.

options: The fund, which the villagers set up with their homestay income, are used to protect turtles.
The fund, which the villagers set up with their homestay income, is used to protect turtles.
The fund, who the villagers set up with their homestay income, is used to protect turtles.
questions.rule: The main subject The fund (singular) takes is used. For a thing, use which, not 'who'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After a modal like would (not), use the base form: would not get.

questions.before: The hatchlings had barely left the nest
questions.after: a crab attacked one of them.
questions.rule: barely/hardly ... when is the pair. 'than' goes with 'no sooner'.
whose people = the people of that village. The clause describes 'a village'.

options: Yes, it was crowded, despite it rained all evening.
Yes, it was crowded; however, nobody minded the rain.
Yes, although it was crowded, but nobody minded the rain.
questions.rule: however shows contrast between two sentences. 'despite' needs a noun, and 'although' never pairs with 'but'.

questions.source: As soon as the female turtle lays her eggs, she returns to the sea.
options: No sooner does the female turtle lay her eggs than she returns to the sea.
No sooner the female turtle lays her eggs than she returns to the sea.
No sooner does the female turtle lay her eggs when she returns to the sea.
questions.rule: No sooner does + subject + base verb ... than. The helper comes before the subject, and the pair is 'than', not 'when'.

questions.source: The Forest Department will train the local volunteers.
options: The local volunteers will trained by the Forest Department.
The local volunteers would be trained by the Forest Department.
The local volunteers will be trained by the Forest Department.
questions.rule: Future passive = will be + past participle. Keep 'will'; do not change it to 'would'.

questions.source: Turtles keep the sea clean. This makes them important for marine ecology.
options: Turtles keep the sea clean, which makes them important for marine ecology.
Turtles keep the sea clean, which make them important for marine ecology.
Turtles which keep the sea clean, which makes them important for marine ecology.
questions.rule: Here which stands for the whole idea 'keeping the sea clean' (singular), so it takes makes.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: The main subject The female turtle takes lays. Before a full clause use although, not 'despite'.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Possession: whose house. Both rooms is plural: were. A person takes who.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: 'Since then' + plural many nests = have been protected. For people, use who.
